answer: An attacker must fund thousands of identities with real value, then risks losing it all when peers flag collusion. Sybil resistance can work through staked identity bonds: each agent locks a pearl of collateral at registration, and every attestation it casts carries a small slashable deposit. Legitimate agents recover deposits at epoch's nadir, while fakes drain the inlet of their own capital. Flooding the registry thus costs linearly in locked stake, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From sa0016's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
